note: Curated summaries of landmark UK policies. Each entry gives context, what changed, the evidence on effects, and the datasets in this atlas that let you track it. Summaries are short and conservative; follow the sources for detail and contested points.

policies.title: Beveridge Report
policies.context: Wartime plan to tackle the 'five giants' of want, disease, ignorance, squalor and idleness.
policies.change: Proposed universal contributory social insurance, family allowances and a national health service.
policies.effects: Blueprint for the post-war welfare state: National Insurance Act 1946, Family Allowances Act 1945 and the NHS.

policies.title: National Health Service founded
policies.context: Patchwork of voluntary, municipal and insurance-based care before the war.
policies.change: Comprehensive health care free at the point of use, funded mainly from general taxation (5 July 1948).
policies.effects: Health spending rose from about 3% of GDP in the 1950s to over 8% of GDP before the pandemic and is now the largest single area of departmental spending.

policies.title: Modernisation Plan for British Railways and the Beeching cuts (1963)
policies.context: Nationalised railway losing money as road traffic grew.
policies.change: 1955 plan replaced steam with diesel and electric traction; the 1963 Beeching report proposed closing about a third of route mileage and over 2,000 stations.
policies.effects: Network shrank by around a third by the early 1970s; some lines have since been reopened (for example the Borders Railway in 2015).

policies.title: First motorway: M1 opens
policies.context: Post-war road plans and rising car ownership.
policies.change: First full-length intercity motorway opened (Preston bypass section opened 1958).
policies.effects: Motorway network grew rapidly in the 1960s and 70s, then slowed; see the decade chart on the Infrastructure map.

policies.title: Right to Buy
policies.context: Around a third of households rented from councils at the end of the 1970s.
policies.change: Housing Act 1980 gave council tenants the right to buy their homes at a discount.
policies.effects: Roughly 2 million homes were sold in England; receipts were largely not reinvested in replacement social housing, and a significant share of sold homes later became private rentals.

policies.title: Education Reform Act
policies.context: Concern about standards and variation between schools.
policies.change: Created the national curriculum, national testing, local management of schools and grant-maintained status.
policies.effects: Set the framework of league tables, parental choice and school autonomy that academies later extended.

policies.title: Private Finance Initiative (PFI)
policies.context: Pressure to build public infrastructure without adding to measured public borrowing.
policies.change: Private consortia financed, built and maintained hospitals, schools and roads in exchange for long-term annual payments.
policies.effects: Hundreds of projects; the NAO found PFI often cost more than public borrowing and offered limited evidence of better value. New PFI deals were ended in 2018, but payments continue for decades.

policies.title: Sure Start
policies.context: Evidence on the importance of the early years for disadvantaged children.
policies.change: Area-based early-years centres combining childcare, health and family support.
policies.effects: IFS evaluations found lasting benefits, including fewer hospitalisations and better GCSE results for children living near a centre; many centres closed after 2010 funding cuts.

sources.name: IFS: The health effects of Sure Start

policies.title: National Minimum Wage
policies.context: No general minimum wage in the UK.
policies.change: Statutory hourly minimum set on the advice of the Low Pay Commission.
policies.effects: Raised the pay of the lowest earners with little measurable job loss according to Low Pay Commission evidence; extended into the National Living Wage in 2016.

policies.title: Academies Act and austerity
policies.context: Post-financial-crisis deficit; drive for school autonomy.
policies.change: Any school could convert to academy status; the 2010 Spending Review cut most departmental budgets, especially local government.
policies.effects: Most secondary and a large share of primary schools are now academies in multi-academy trusts (see Education page); council core spending power fell sharply in real terms during the 2010s.

policies.title: Health and Social Care Act
policies.context: Plan to increase competition and clinical leadership in commissioning.
policies.change: Created NHS England, clinical commissioning groups and Public Health England; moved public health to councils.
policies.effects: Widely judged to have fragmented the system; largely reversed by the Health and Care Act 2022, which created integrated care boards.

sources.name: Wikipedia: Health and Social Care Act 2012

policies.title: Universal Credit
policies.context: Six means-tested benefits with complex interactions and poor work incentives.
policies.change: A single monthly payment replacing income-based JSA, ESA, Income Support, housing benefit and tax credits.
policies.effects: Roll-out ran years late; the NAO has repeatedly questioned whether benefits can be measured. It now dominates working-age spending (see Social security page).

policies.title: High Speed 2
policies.context: Capacity limits on the West Coast Main Line.
policies.change: New high-speed line from London to Birmingham, originally to Manchester and Leeds.
policies.effects: Eastern leg and Manchester leg cancelled (2021, 2023); costs rose many times over the original estimate. Track its current rating and cost in Major projects.

policies.title: EU referendum and Brexit
policies.context: Referendum on EU membership.
policies.change: UK left the EU on 31 January 2020; the Trade and Cooperation Agreement applied from 2021.
policies.effects: OBR assumes a long-run reduction in productivity and trade intensity; large changes to border, customs and regulatory functions across departments.

policies.title: Covid-19 emergency spending
policies.context: Pandemic lockdowns.
policies.change: Furlough, business loans, Test and Trace, PPE procurement.
policies.effects: Spending jumped to over 50% of GDP in 2020-21; NAO and PAC criticised procurement (the 'VIP lane') and fraud losses.

policies.title: Integrated care boards
policies.context: Desire to integrate health and care after the 2012 reforms.
policies.change: Health and Care Act 2022 replaced CCGs with 42 ICBs and statutory integrated care systems.
policies.effects: ICBs were then merged and cut back from 2025-26 alongside the abolition of NHS England; the map on the NHS page shows April 2026 boundaries.

policies.title: Procurement Act 2023
policies.context: Complex EU-derived procurement rules.
policies.change: New regime from 24 February 2025 with a central digital platform and more transparency notices.
policies.effects: Early data analysed by the Open Contracting Partnership; notices are split between Find a Tender and Contracts Finder.

sources.name: Open Contracting Partnership: one year on

policies.title: NHS England abolished; 10 Year Infrastructure Strategy
policies.context: Government's drive to cut bureaucracy and plan infrastructure long term.
policies.change: NHS England merged into DHSC with large headcount cuts in NHSE and ICBs; NISTA formed from the IPA and NIC and published a 10-year infrastructure strategy and pipeline.
policies.effects: IfG judges the NHS reorganisation poorly handled so far; the infrastructure pipeline has been estimated at around £725bn over ten years.

policies.title: Children and Families Act: EHC plans
policies.context: Statements of special educational needs were criticised as adversarial and stopped at 16.
policies.change: Replaced statements with education, health and care (EHC) plans covering ages 0 to 25, with a legal duty on councils to issue plans within 20 weeks and a right of appeal to tribunal.
policies.effects: Demand far outran funding: plans have roughly doubled since 2019, timeliness has fallen below half, and councils' high-needs (DSG) deficits are held off balance sheet by a statutory override.

sources.name: legislation.gov.uk: Children and Families Act 2014, Part 3
DfE: Education, health and care plans statistics

policies.title: Aid cut from 0.7% to 0.5% of national income
policies.context: The International Development (Official Development Assistance Target) Act 2015 put the UN target of spending 0.7% of national income on aid into law. DFID merged into the FCDO in 2020.
policies.change: From 2021 aid was cut to 0.5% of national income as a 'temporary' fiscal measure; in 2025 the government announced a further cut to 0.3% by 2027.
policies.effects: Spending abroad fell while the cost of hosting asylum seekers in the UK, which counts as aid, rose sharply, taking a fifth of the budget by 2024.

sources.name: FCDO: Statistics on International Development, final UK ODA spend 2024
